transcript.text: This could be something simple such as the child lock being on, a power/isolation issue, or—if it is induction—a pan not being recognised. If only one zone is affected, it is more likely to be that zone’s element/control (or, on induction, its coil or power module). First, check whether a key or padlock symbol is lit. If so, try holding that control for a few seconds to unlock it, then retry a zone. Also, if the whole hob appears dead, check the wall isolator switch is on and see whether a circuit breaker has tripped. Do not keep resetting a breaker if it trips again. Is it an induction hob (glass surface that heats the pan rather than glowing red), ceramic/halogen glass hob, or solid electric plates—and what exactly happens: are all zones affected or only one, do any lights/error symbols show, and does it fail to heat, not switch on, or keep cutting out?
It's a ceramic one, glass top that glows red. Only the rear right zone isn't working, the other three are fine. The display shows the number for it but it doesn't heat up.

This is unlikely to be the supply or a general lock. The most likely fault is the rear-right radiant element itself; next most likely is that zone’s control switch/electronic output. A connection underneath is also possible. 1. With the hob cool, check the glass over and around that zone for any crack. If there is one, stop using the hob and arrange repair��moisture can reach electrical parts beneath.
2. If the glass is intact, use a pan with a little water and set that zone to maximum for a few minutes. If it stays completely cold while the other zones heat normally, it supports an element/control fault rather than a setting issue.
3. Switch the hob off at its isolator before any further inspection; do not remove the hob or access wiring yourself. Does it have individual knobs or touch controls, and does the rear-right zone remain completely cold on maximum? That will help distinguish the control from the heating element, although either normally needs an engineer to access safely.
It's touch controls. The zone stays completely cold, no red glow at all, and the glass isn't cracked as far as I can see. It was slow to heat for a while before it stopped last week.

The rear-right radiant heating element is the most likely fault. The display accepting the setting shows the touch controls are responding, while no glow or heat from that one zone points to the element circuit. Its earlier slow heating makes an element failing progressively more likely than a sudden settings issue. The alternatives are a burnt/loose connection beneath the glass or a failed output on the control board for that zone. An engineer would confirm this with the hob isolated, then test the element and its connections for continuity before fitting anything. Keep using the other zones only if they are behaving normally, but leave the failed zone switched off. Do not remove the glass or attempt wiring checks yourself: ceramic hobs are mains-wired and access involves lifting the hob and working around live-supply connections. If the repair quote is for the radiant element alone it is commonly a sensible repair; a control board can make the decision more dependent on the hob’s age and condition.
